newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar retreats slightly by Tokyo noon, still firm.
newsitem.headline: Dollar retreats slightly by Tokyo noon, still firm.

text.p: 0300 GMT TRADED HI/LO AS OF 0300 GMT
The dollar had retreated slightly by Tokyo midday on Wednesday but held its own above 114 yen after rising more than one yen, mainly on short-covering.

Comments by Japan Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka added momentum to the short-covering, with no impact seen from Tuesday's U.S. decision to leave interest rates steady. Gains were capped by exporter and interbank sales near 114.50 yen.

The dollar also received a boost from active short-covering of marks for yen, mainly from trust banks who had sold heavily on Tuesday, with stop-loss buy orders also kicking in around 68.00 yen, dealers said.

Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee on Wednesday that worries over an excessive weakening of the yen have completely disappeared. "A stable currency market is important for the economy. Excessive strengthening of the yen as well as excessive weakening of the yen is undesirable," he said.
He added that Japan will deal in a "timely and appropriate way" with foreign exchange volatility and excessive movements.

Although short-covering since early morning had been pushing the greenback steadily higher, Mitsuzuka's comments gave it additional upward impetus, enabling it to briefly touch 114.50 yen before falling back in the face of offers from interbank operators and exporters.
Trust banks, who had been selling dollars for yen heavily as the greenback fell, aggressively covered short positions this morning, along with interbank operators, dealers said.
"The market has taken heart from yesterday's comments from (Eisuke) Sakakibara and the dollar's failure to fall further in overnight trade," one dealer said.

The greenback fell as low as 111.98 yen in late Tokyo trade on Tuesday but ended New York trade at 112.58/68 yen. Its slide appeared to have been halted mainly by comments by Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, who said the pace of the yen's strengthening was too rapid and that too much volatility in foreign exchange markets was undesirable.

A trust bank dealer said the downside appeared to be solid for now near 113.80 yen, with any substantial dips inviting bargain-hunting. "The dollar is likely to fluctuate between 113.80 yen and 114.50 yen this afternoon," he added.
The mark was moving volatilely against the yen, rising to around 68.30 yen at one point before falling back. At 0329 GMT it stood around 67.95/98 yen, well above its low of around 67.23 yen.
The trust bank dealer said the mark/yen surge had originally led the dollar higher, but volume was greater in dollar/yen trade.

The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided Tuesday to leave U.S. rates unchanged, but because this had been mostly digested in overseas trade it had virtually no impact in Tokyo, dealers said.
